voice.openaiKeyDesc2: Paste it once below. It is encrypted on this machine and never shown again — each voice session mints its own short-lived token from it, and the key itself never leaves your computer. It is the same OpenAI key listed under Agents & Models; setting it in either place is enough.

voice.idleDisconnectDesc: How long the voice session stays open with no talking before it auto-closes. The spend cap still stops a runaway session even when this is off.

titles.homePlain: STEP 1 OF 4 · A HOME FOR THE APP

persona.headline: A CLONE OF YOU, WORKING 24/7
persona.body: Munder Difflin turns the CLI agent you already use into a clone of you — one that runs an office of long-running agents and keeps working while you're away. It manages everything around them: context, memory, tasks, triggers, environment, files, and integrations.
persona.ask: FIRST — WHO ARE YOU? (we'll tailor the setup)
persona.technicalDesc: I write code or work in a terminal. Show me CLI commands, flags, and model ids.
persona.nonTechnicalDesc: I'm in marketing, sales, ops, or just starting out. Explain things in plain language.

welcome.headline: YOUR CLONE AND THE FLOOR IT RUNS
welcome.descPlain: Your clone runs a small office of AI workers, and you watch it all from one screen. Here's what's inside:
welcome.desc: Your clone coordinates a hive of AI coding agents — persistent, watchable, all local. Here's what's inside:

engines.label: TEN ENGINES, ONE OFFICE
engines.desc: Claude Code, Codex, Grok, Kimi, Antigravity, Qwen, OpenCode, Crush, pi & Copilot — live agents on one floor.
engines.descPlain: Ten AI assistants — Claude, Codex, Gemini, Grok and more — working side by side in one shared office.

clone.label: MICHAEL IS YOUR CLONE
clone.desc: Your clone runs the floor — triages requests, routes tasks, and escalates only what needs you.
clone.descPlain: Your clone, Michael, takes your requests, hands work to the right agent, and only interrupts you when it matters.

memory.label: LONG-TERM MEMORY
memory.desc: Each agent keeps notes, mined into a shared, searchable MemPalace.
memory.descPlain: Agents remember what they've done, so they don't start from scratch every time.

commandCenter.label: COMMAND CENTER
commandCenter.desc: Terminal · Floor · Memory · Activity · Tasks · Triggers in one control surface.
commandCenter.descPlain: One dashboard to watch the work, the agents' memory, tasks, and triggers.

guardrails.label: GUARDRAILS
guardrails.desc: Per-agent token budgets, a steer→constrain→stop circuit breaker, and human approvals.
guardrails.descPlain: Spending limits and safety stops keep agents in check — and they can ask you before big actions.

hires.label: READY-MADE HIRES
hires.desc: Grab a pre-configured agent from the Agent Gallery and spawn it in one click.
hires.descPlain: Hire a ready-made agent from the gallery in one click — no setup needed.

providerBlurb.qwen: Qwen — runs a local Qwen model on your machine

home.descPlain: Create a new, empty folder for the app to call home. Everything the app remembers — its own settings and your agents' memory — is stored here. Something like ~/HarnessAgents works well. We'll create it for you if it doesn't exist.
home.desc: Pick a folder where the harness will keep its own files — agent metadata, logs, and any new repos you create from here. Something like ~/HarnessAgents is a fine default. We'll create it if it doesn't exist.
home.notePlain: You won't need to open this folder day-to-day — it's just where the app keeps its notes so nothing is lost when you restart.
home.note: Think of this as the "town hall." The harness pins agent state there so sessions can be picked back up after a restart.

orchestrator.descPlain: Michael is your clone — he reads your requests, breaks them into tasks, and hands them to the right agent. He's the boss of the floor; you're still the boss of him. Choose which AI engine powers him.
orchestrator.desc: Michael is your clone — the boss of the floor you just met. He triages your requests, assigns tasks, and manages the team, while escalating anything that genuinely needs you. Pick the engine and model that power him; give him a longer-context, higher-capability model.
orchestrator.cliAgentPlain: A CLI agent is an AI coding assistant that runs on your computer — popular ones are Claude Code (Anthropic), Codex (OpenAI) and Antigravity (Google Gemini). Your clone is the always-on one that runs your whole office. We recommend Claude Code on Opus 4.8 (1M). You can add or switch the others later.
orchestrator.cliAgent: Each option is a CLI engine you have installed (Claude Code, Codex, Antigravity/Gemini, or a local proxy like Qwen). Your clone (Michael) is the engine that orchestrates the whole hive. Recommended: Claude Code · Opus 4.8 · 1M — other providers can be wired per agent later.
orchestrator.modelNote: This only sets Michael's engine. You can run other providers per agent later.

repos.descPlain: Add your projects. A project is simply a folder — it can hold code, documents, notes, or any files you want your agents to work with. You can create a brand-new folder or pick an existing one, and add more anytime.
repos.desc: Add the repos you want your agents to work in. Each folder becomes a project (a room on the floor) — multiple agents can share one. You can add more later.
repos.emptyPlain: No projects added yet. Optional — you can add one later.
repos.empty: No repos added yet. Optional, but recommended.

permissions.autonomyHead: HOW MUCH CAN AGENTS DO ON THEIR OWN?
permissions.autoLabelPlain: LET AGENTS WORK ON THEIR OWN
permissions.autoOnPlain: On. Agents carry out tasks without stopping to ask — the smoothest experience.
permissions.autoOffPlain: Off. Agents pause and ask you before changing files or running commands.
permissions.autoOn: On. Agents never pause — Claude runs bypassPermissions, Codex bypasses approvals + sandbox, etc.
permissions.autoOff: Off. Each agent asks before edits / shell commands (Claude default, codex -a untrusted, …).
permissions.autoNotePlain: Best when agents work in their own projects. You can change this later, including for individual agents.
permissions.autoNote: The right default for the "control room" experience; a foot-gun on production repos. Override per agent in the Add Agent dialog.
permissions.reliabilityHead: KEEP THINGS RUNNING WHILE YOU'RE AWAY
permissions.reliabilityDescPlain: Your agents keep working on a schedule and in live terminals, even when you step away. These settings keep you in the loop and keep things running.
permissions.reliabilityDesc: Your agents keep working on a schedule and in live terminals. If your Mac fully sleeps those timers pause and catch up the moment you're back — nothing is lost, it may just run late.
permissions.keepAwakeDesc: Strong keep-alive: stops your Mac from sleeping while an agent is live, so schedules and terminals fire on time even when you step away. Uses more battery — best on power. Off by default.
permissions.notificationsDesc: Get pinged when an agent needs you or a terminal needs reviving — even while you're away. macOS asks permission the first time one fires.
permissions.openAtLoginDesc: Relaunch the harness after a reboot so scheduled missions resume on their own. No prompt — applies immediately.
permissions.shareStatsDesc: A handful of anonymous events (app opened, agent spawned, feature used) that help improve Munder Difflin — never prompts, code, file paths, or agent output. Full list in TELEMETRY.md; change anytime in Settings.
permissions.stayAwakeDesc: macOS only lets you set this one yourself. In Battery → Options, turn on "Prevent automatic sleeping when the display is off" (on power adapter) so timers keep firing with the display asleep. Without a sleep-preventing setting the Mac still truly sleeps — work survives and catches up on wake.
